content.overview: Section 2 contains the interpretive definitions used in the Act and sets the territorial/application framework for Part I and specified other provisions. Definitions must be applied in their statutory context, including qualifications in section 2(1) and the application provisions in section 2(2)–(5).
content.glance: Statutory definitions control meaning; arbitration agreement is linked to s. 7; international commercial arbitration has exact foreign-party and commercial tests.
content.study: Section 2(1) defines arbitration, arbitration agreement, arbitral award, arbitral tribunal, court, international commercial arbitration, legal representative, party and related expressions. ‘Arbitration agreement’ is expressly tied to section 7. Sections 2(2)–(5) regulate application of Part I and must be checked before assuming every Part I provision applies identically.

sections.heading: Section 2(1) definitions
sections.body: Principal statutory definitions for expressions used in the Act; do not substitute textbook meanings.

sections.heading: Arbitration and arbitration agreement
sections.body: ‘Arbitration’ is defined broadly; ‘arbitration agreement’ is linked to section 7 and must be tested under that section.

sections.heading: Court and international commercial arbitration
sections.body: ‘Court’ identifies the judicial forum by subject-matter rules; international commercial arbitration requires the statutory foreign-party and commercial criteria.

sections.heading: Sections 2(2)–(5) application framework
sections.body: These sub-sections regulate application of Part I and related arrangements; check them before mechanical application of Part I.

examples.title: Arbitration agreement
examples.body: A contract clause referring disputes to arbitration must be tested under section 7; section 2(1)(b) supplies the definitional link.

examples.title: International commercial arbitration
examples.body: Apply every element of section 2(1)(f) rather than treating any foreign connection as automatically sufficient.

hypotheticals.question: Is any written reference to arbitration automatically an arbitration agreement under section 2?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 2(1)(b) refers to section 7; the agreement must be tested under section 7.

rows.right: Creates or regulates the particular right or procedure

misconceptions.trap: Using a textbook meaning instead of the statutory definition.
misconceptions.correction: Start with the exact definition in section 2 and its qualifications.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should section 2 be used?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify the expression in issue, state its section 2 definition, read any qualification, then apply the operative provision. For an arbitration agreement, read s. 2(1)(b) with s. 7.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Definitions control meaning but do not replace operative provisions.

examTips: Do not treat s. 2(1)(b) as a substitute for s. 7.
For ICA, map each statutory criterion to the facts.

enhancement.definition: Section 2 supplies statutory definitions and the Part I application framework.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Apply statutory definitions in context; arbitration agreement links to s. 7.

shortAnswer.answer: The definitions and application framework provision of the Act.
shortAnswer.method: State role and link to operative sections.

tenMark.point: State the role of section 2 definitions in interpreting the Act
tenMark.application: Apply the relevant definition to the facts before invoking later operative sections.

tenMark.point: Identify which definitions apply only to Part I or to the whole Act
tenMark.application: Check territorial and Part-scope qualifications in s. 2 before treating a term as universal.

tenMark.point: Distinguish arbitration agreement, arbitral tribunal and court under s. 2
tenMark.application: Map each defined term to the procedural step in issue.

tenMark.point: Apply international commercial arbitration definition where foreign elements exist
tenMark.application: Test place of business, nationality and subject-matter criteria before labelling the dispute international.

sixteenMark.point: Explain how section 2 structures interpretation of the entire Act
sixteenMark.application: Open with the definition, apply qualifications, then link to the operative provision.

sixteenMark.point: Analyse Part-scope limitations on selected definitions
sixteenMark.application: Separate whole-Act definitions from Part I-only meanings.

sixteenMark.point: Work a problem involving court and arbitral tribunal under s. 2
sixteenMark.application: Identify the competent forum using the statutory definitions, not common usage.

sixteenMark.point: Assess whether a dispute is an international commercial arbitration under s. 2
sixteenMark.application: Apply the statutory tests to the parties and subject matter.

sixteenMark.point: Conclude with limits of definitional provisions
sixteenMark.application: Definitions do not create substantive rights; they control meaning of operative sections.
